Evidence-Based Martial Arts

Training Sources & Research

We ground our coaching in peer-reviewed motor learning research, youth sports safety studies, dojo lineage, and local community partnerships.

Pillar 1

Peer-Reviewed Movement Science & Sports Medicine

Published clinical trials, systematic reviews, and biomechanical investigations supporting safe skill development, motor learning, and youth sports longevity.

Academic Research

Games-Based Teaching & Motor Learning Review

Systematic review showing how small learning games build motor skill, agile footwork, and fast decision-making.

Read research summary →
Academic Research

BJJ School Randomized Controlled Trial

Randomized trial measuring how school Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu builds attention, emotional calm, and teamwork in class.

Read research summary →
Sports Medicine

BJJ Injury Rates (2025)

A survey of 881 practitioners reported 5.5 injuries per 1,000 training hours. It did not test prevention methods or youth injury rates.

Read research summary →
Academic Research

Deliberate Practice & Sport Performance

A meta-analysis found deliberate practice explained 18% of differences in sports performance. Other factors also mattered.

Read the research →
Sports Medicine

Pediatric BJJ Injury Visits

A U.S. study of emergency-department records from 2012–2021 describes child BJJ injuries. It does not show risk per class or test prevention.

Read the research →
Local Public Health

Greene County Public Health Report (2024)

The report records Greene County’s 2024 community health assessment work and a joint health plan with Columbia County.

Read the county report →
Sports Medicine

Overuse Injuries in Young Athletes

The American Academy of Pediatrics reviews overuse injuries, training load, recovery, and burnout in young athletes.

Read the clinical report →
Sports Medicine

Concussion Care in Combat Sports

Ringside physicians outline concussion care and return-to-competition guidance for combat sports. This is not a school-class safety protocol.

Read the consensus statement →
Academic Research

Aerobic Exercise, Learning & Cognition

This review looks at aerobic exercise, brain plasticity, learning, and cognition. It does not study Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

Read the research →
Sports Medicine

BJJ Injury Epidemiology Review (2024)

A review of seven studies with 2,847 practitioners found that knee, chest and rib, and shoulder injuries were often reported.

Read the research →

Responsible Evidence Usage

How We Use Evidence: Studies examine specific populations and environments. They inform our safety standards and teaching progression, but individual athletic development is always coached at a personal pace.
